newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico outlines corn sales subsidies for '97 crop.
newsitem.headline: Mexico outlines corn sales subsidies for '97 crop.

text.p: Mexico's Agriculture Ministry outlined Friday a subsidy mechanism it has put in place to facilitate corn sales between growers and millers from this 1996-1997 autumn-winter crop.

Via the government's Official Gazette, the ministry said the government will pay support to growers worked out from the difference between the set producer floor price in each state and a reference price calculated by the government staples agency Conasupo based on CBOT futures prices.

Premium prices will also be paid to growers on proof that millers paid above floor levels for quality grain, the ministry added. Maximum premiums will be 25 pesos per tonne for corn with 0.0 percent and 3.3 percent damage.

Also, premiums will be paid to millers of 112.50 pesos per tonne for every tonne bought over and above millers' needs in the May 1-Sept 30 period, the ministry said. The government has set a ceiling of 959,488 tonnes for corn that is subject to the millers' premium.

Mexico has initiated a number of subsidy mechanisms to facilitate internal grains transactions between growers and millers. It sets floor prices for growers in each state via Conasupo, which guarantees all corn grown will be sold.
Mexico's autumn-winter cycle refers to the planting period. Grains are harvested in the summer months.
